chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Naḍr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
Al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, while I was with him, about performing sajdah on al-qufr and on al-qīr. He said: There is no harm.
So the correct approach regarding this narration is that we interpret it as applying to a state of necessity or taqiyyah, not to a state of choice.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary concealment for protection
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: necessity; a constrained circumstance affecting legal application
key_terms.الِاخْتِيَارِ: a state of free choice, without coercion or necessity
key_terms.الْقُفْرِ: a surface referred to in the narration as a material upon which sajdah was asked about
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Can sajdah be performed on pitch or similar surfaces according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing sajdah on tar-like or pitch-like surfaces and another surface described as al-qufr. Although the Imam عليه السلام says there is no harm, the narration is understood in Shia legal tradition as applying in cases of necessity or taqiyyah rather than in ordinary circumstances of free choice.
